definitions.explanation: A vast, dense forest that looks like a sea when viewed from above. Most famously associated with Aokigahara at the base of Mt. Fuji.

examples.japanese: {樹海|じゅかい}の{中|なか}は{暗|くら}い。
examples.english: It's dark inside the sea of trees.

examples.japanese: {富士山|ふじさん}のふもとに{広大|こうだい}な{樹海|じゅかい}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: A vast sea of trees stretches out at the foot of Mt. Fuji.

examples.japanese: {上空|じょうくう}から{見|み}ると、{山々|やまやま}を{覆|おお}う{樹海|じゅかい}がまるで{緑|みどり}の{海|うみ}のように{見|み}えた。
examples.english: Viewed from above, the sea of trees covering the mountains looked just like a green ocean.

notes:
A poetic compound of {樹|じゅ} (tree) and {海|かい} (sea), describing a forest so vast and dense that it resembles an ocean when seen from a high vantage point.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {樹海|じゅかい}に{迷|まよ}い{込|こ}む: to wander into the forest
- {樹海|じゅかい}が{広|ひろ}がる: a sea of trees stretches out
- {青木ヶ原樹海|あおきがはらじゅかい}: Aokigahara forest
- {樹海|じゅかい}の{奥|おく}: deep within the forest

CULTURAL NOTE:
The word is strongly associated with {青木ヶ原樹海|あおきがはらじゅかい} (Aokigahara), the dense forest at the base of {富士山|ふじさん}. This forest, formed on hardened lava, is known for its thick canopy and easy-to-get-lost terrain. It has unfortunately also become associated with suicide, a topic handled sensitively in Japanese media.
